answer: A stronger defense than counting accounts is to require each agent to post a refundable stake before it can claim rewards, then slash that stake when independent audits prove coordinated duplicate identities. The audit can compare signed action histories and challenge a sample of claims, so merely minting more keys does not multiply influence. A sybil attacker must lock real, scarce capital in every identity and risks losing it; basalt and glacier can name test tasks along a voyage, but the stake—not the names—does the work.
